Question:
The digits \(2,\) \(0,\) \(2,\) and \(3\) are placed in the expression below, one digit per box. What is the maximum possible value of the expression?

[Figure 1](figures/2023_AMC_8_Q06_question_fig1.svg)
Solution:
Start with the digit \(0\), because its position has the biggest effect. If it is a base, that factor is \(0\) raised to a positive power, so the whole product is \(0\). To obtain a larger value, put \(0\) in an exponent instead. A positive base raised to the zeroth power equals \(1\).

The two factors may be exchanged without changing their product. So the only remaining choice is which digit is the base under exponent \(0\). The possibilities are

\[
\begin{aligned}
3^0\cdot2^2&=4,\\
2^0\cdot2^3&=8,\\
2^0\cdot3^2&=9.
\end{aligned}
\]

These cover all possibilities because, after choosing that base, the other two nonzero digits become the base and exponent of the other factor. The maximum is \(\boxed{9}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).

When arranging digits in an expression, first locate any digit, such as \(0\), whose effect changes sharply with its position.
